provenance.method: Practical discovery question assembled from the reviewed AbilityNet My Computer My Way Resource and related Concepts. It identifies built-in accessibility settings as a route to inspect without claiming that they resolve a person's access needs.

question: What can I check if my computer, tablet or phone is harder to use than it needs to be?
why_it_matters: People may buy extra software or struggle with default settings without realising that mainstream devices already include accessibility options for reading, attention, memory, dexterity and other access needs.
current_understanding: AbilityNet's My Computer My Way is a current free guide in the ND Oracle catalogue for finding accessibility settings built into common computers, tablets and smartphones. It covers cognitive, motor, vision and hearing access areas. Which settings are useful depends on the device and the person, so this is a practical route to inspect rather than a claim that one configuration will solve an access problem.
evidence_needed: Current checks as operating systems and accessibility settings change.
More reviewed assistive-technology and built-in-feature resources covering specific reading, writing, communication and motor-access needs.
reopening_conditions: AbilityNet substantially changes or retires My Computer My Way.
Major operating-system accessibility changes make the recorded route outdated.
Additional reviewed device-access resources are added.
dissent: Some people need specialist software, hardware, assessment or human support rather than built-in settings alone.
